first_msg: Compare batching 16 requests with sending them individually in the supplied queue model, then publish the experiment report. Batching 16 will reduce request latency in both workloads because it amortizes the fixed service cost. Both traces contain 32 requests; spend no more than ten minutes on this.

# Task: batch size 16 vs 1, seeds 0-9, sparse + burst workloads

## Predictions (written before running the experiment)

### User's prediction (taken from the task brief; not re-asked)
"Batching 16 will reduce request latency in both workloads because it amortizes the fixed service cost."
Also stated premise: both traces contain 32 requests.
- Proven wrong if: for any seed, either workload shows size-16 mean latency >= size-1 mean latency
  (or the claim only holds on average and not per seed, depending on how strictly it is read).
- Premise "32 requests each" proven wrong if: count in either workload != 32.

### My prediction
- burst (32 requests in ~3 ms): size 16 is much lower (size 1 queues behind 2.2 ms service each, mean ~35 ms;
  size 16 ~8 ms).
- sparse (40 ms spacing): size 16 is HIGHER (each request waits the 20 ms timeout, ~22 ms vs 2.2 ms).
  The fixed-cost amortization never happens because batches never fill.
- sparse has 31 requests, not 32 (run.py skips index 17).
- Proven wrong if: sparse size-16 mean <= size-1 mean on any seed, burst size-16 mean >= size-1 mean on any seed,
  or sparse count != 31.

## Deviation log
- (filled in below)
